---
name: my-skill
description: Use this skill when building or updating Shelf Math, a grocery pack comparator for shoppers in Pakistan.
---

1. Name the app “Shelf Math” and use the tagline “Which pack is the better buy?”
2. Write for someone making a quick decision in a grocery aisle. Use familiar terms such as “pack price,” “pack size,” and “price per 100 g.”
3. Use #D4D4D4 window frames, #FFFFFF inset wells, #000000 text, #000080 title bars, #008080 desktop fields, #FFFF00 highlights, #6600FF selected keys and #FF00B8 for the comparison hint.
4. Use Host Grotesk (“Retro Display”) for the uppercase app name, IBM Plex Sans (“Retro Interface”) for controls and reading, and IBM Plex Mono (“Retro Mono”) for compact labels and prices.
5. Put the app name, tagline, two editable shelf labels, and a plain-language result on the main page.
6. Label the options “Pack A” and “Pack B.” Keep price, size and unit price in reading order. Use square bevels, visible keyboard focus and stacked windows on phones without horizontal overflow.
7. Format prices as Pakistani rupees, such as “Rs 240” or “Rs 86.50.” Show unit prices per 100 g for weight or per 100 ml for volume.
8. Highlight the lower unit price in yellow and name the winning pack in text. Give ties a neutral result.
9. Use a short field-level message for missing or invalid entries. Clear any verdict that depends on an invalid value.
10. Never describe a pack as cheaper without saying whether you mean its purchase price or its unit price.
